hypotheses.justification: With hb deleted, split on b ≥ 0. In the other case put c = -b > 0 and u = -t. The quadratic hypothesis gives c(1 + u²) ≤ d*u, so u > 0 and c*u² - d*u + c ≤ 0. This implies d² - 4*c² ≥ 0 and u ≥ 2*c/(d + Real.sqrt (d² - 4*c²)); negating gives the desired bound on t. The stated root is then exactly -2*c/(d + Real.sqrt (d² - 4*c²)).
With hd deleted, hb and hsmall imply 0 ≤ 2*b < d, hence 0 < d. The original proof can then proceed with this derived positivity.

With hsmall deleted, split on whether 2*b < d. In that case use the original argument. Otherwise, hb and hd give d ≤ 2*b, hence d² - 4*b² ≤ 0. Mathlib defines Real.sqrt to be zero on nonpositive inputs (Real.sqrt_eq_zero_of_nonpos), so the right-hand side is 2*b/d ≥ 1; ht1 gives t < 1, proving the bound directly.
